source_clauses: I need a compact folding stand for my desk.
It should have three legs that fold in close to the body, so the whole thing becomes narrow and compact when I put it away.
Everything should stay attached while it is folded.
I do not want to take anything off to fold it, or loose pieces to look after.
When I want to use it, I should be able to open it by hand, following a sequence that makes sense as I go.
The three legs should end up spread apart in different directions so they give the stand a usable footprint on the desk.
Nothing should come apart or fall off while I am opening it, and I should not need tools, a motor, or any other equipment to do it.
Once it is open, it needs to stay open on its own.
I should not have to hold the legs while I use it, and they should not be able to fold back, twist aside, or come off.
Nothing should turn on its own, shift out of place, or move in some other direction I was not expecting.
Before it can be folded again I want to have to do something deliberate, so it does not collapse just because I knocked it.
After that deliberate release, it should fold back down to the same compact shape it started in.
The opening and folding sequence should be repeatable, with all normal parts remaining attached and without anything needing to be removed and put back on.
It is meant to hold a small object on my desk while I am working.
It should also be something that can genuinely be built as a product and put together in a sensible order, and stay together through normal opening and folding.

requirements.statement: The stand is compact and folding for use on a desk.
The stand has three legs.
The legs fold in close to the body when put away.
requirements.notes: No specific distance or angle; 'close' is qualitative.

Everything stays attached while folded.
No loose pieces to look after.
The stand can be opened by hand without tools, motor, or other equipment.
The opening sequence makes sense as the user goes.
When open, the three legs are spread apart in different directions.
When open, the legs provide a usable footprint on the desk.
Nothing comes apart or falls off during opening.
Once open, the stand stays open on its own.
The user does not have to hold the legs while using the stand.
The legs cannot fold back, twist aside, or come off while in use.
Nothing turns on its own, shifts out of place, or moves unexpectedly.
Before folding, the user must perform a deliberate release action.
After the deliberate release, the stand folds back to the same compact shape.
The opening and folding sequence is repeatable.
All normal parts remain attached during repeatable sequences.
Nothing needs to be removed and put back on during opening and folding.
The stand is meant to hold a small object on a desk while working.
The stand can be genuinely built as a product.
The stand can be put together in a sensible order.
The stand stays together through normal opening and folding.

scenarios.description: User opens the stand by hand from folded to open state, following a sensible sequence, without tools or motor.
scenarios.trigger: User wants to use the stand.

scenarios.description: User uses the stand to hold a small object on the desk while working; the stand remains stable and open.
scenarios.trigger: Object is placed on the stand.

scenarios.description: User deliberately releases the stand to allow folding, then folds it back to the same compact shape.
scenarios.trigger: User wants to put the stand away.

scenarios.description: The stand is put together in a sensible order as part of manufacturing.
The stand is opened and folded repeatedly without needing to remove parts or use tools.
